ownerThemes.theme: Several owner help threads describe top thread looping mid-seam on a new 6700C after a clean test swatch; the answers point to rethreading through the tension discs, cleaning lint from the bobbin area, and the small bobbin case screw.
Walmart owner reviews (4 of 5 stars over about 200 reviews) call it smooth and good for quilting, curtains and clothing, with one experienced sewer saying it is not a first machine.
PatternReview members discussing the launch of Singer's computerized Heavy Duty line note that earlier HD models were all mechanical and question what the electronics add on a budget frame.

crossShop.why: Same head and frame with fewer stitches, no lettering and 5 feet, for about $30 less.
The mechanical Heavy Duty with a walking foot in the box; buyers weigh dials against an LCD.
The step up for quilters who want a wider harp and a knee lifter in a computerized machine.

editorial.verdict: The 6700C is the middle of Singer's computerized Heavy Duty line, adding lettering, a speed slider and a 10-foot kit with a walking foot to the 6600C head while leaving the thread cutter to the 6800C.
editorial.whoFor: A beginner or returning sewer who wants a walking foot, speed control and monogram lettering on a 1,100 spm metal-frame machine under $350.
editorial.skipIf: You want an automatic thread cutter or needle up/down button, or you would rather have dials than menus on a heavy fabric machine.

checks.title: Extension table bundle

checks.title: Applications are not stitches
checks.body: 411 is Singer's count of techniques. Ask the dealer for the stitch chart or check the manual to see the actual pattern list before comparing with a machine that quotes built-in stitches.

faqs.q: How many stitches does the Singer 6700C have?
faqs.a: Singer markets 411 stitch applications, and its own page is quoted at 200 built-in stitch applications. Neither is a plain count of stitch patterns, so we list both and flag the row.

faqs.q: Does the 6700C have an automatic thread cutter?
faqs.a: No. It has a tie-off button. The automatic thread cutter and needle up/down button are 6800C features.

faqs.q: Does the 6700C come with a walking foot?
faqs.a: Yes. The even feed (walking) foot is one of 10 feet on the accessory list, along with open toe and cording feet.
6.4 in (163 mm) from needle to tower, per the Sewing Machines Plus listing.
15.4 lb per the parts dealer. Amazon lists 14.6 lb and one blog 16.3 lb, so treat the figure as approximate.
Yes. A built-in lettering font is listed for monogramming; one comparison site counts 2 fonts.
It has a 6.4 in throat, a walking foot and a speed slider, which suits piecing and small quilts. Owner reviews call it good for quilting; the harp is small for anything larger than a lap quilt.
25 years on the head, 2 years on motor and electronics, 90 days on adjustments and attachments, per Singer's warranty page.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the 6700C and the 6800C?
faqs.a: Same motor, frame and throat. The 6800C adds an automatic thread cutter, needle up/down, start/stop button, stitch memory and more stitches.
